Mahindra Logistics Posts Q2 Net Profit Of ₹26.2 Crore Versus YoY Loss
Mahindra Logistics returned to profitability in Q2 with a net profit of ₹26.2 crore, beating consensus analyst estimates of ₹20.7 crore. Revenue expanded 24.63% YoY to ₹2,100 crore, while EBITDA margin expanded 82 bps YoY to 5.92%.
Sahi Markets
Published: 23 Oct 2026, 02:43 PM IST (1 month ago)
Last Updated: 23 Oct 2026, 02:43 PM IST (1 month ago)
2 min read
Reviewed by Arpit Seth
Share
Market snapshot: Mahindra Logistics Limited declared its Q2 financial results, delivering a consolidated net profit of ₹26.2 crore, turning around from a net loss of ₹10.4 crore in the same period last year. Total revenue for the quarter rose to ₹2,100 crore, supported by operational efficiency and margin improvement.
Data Snapshot
Consolidated Net Profit for Q2 stood at ₹26.2 crore, compared to a net loss of ₹10.4 crore in the prior-year quarter, exceeding analyst expectations of ₹20.7 crore.
Consolidated Revenue from operations reached ₹2,100 crore, rising from ₹1,685 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Consolidated EBITDA reached ₹123 crore, up from ₹85.1 crore YoY.
Consolidated EBITDA Margin expanded to 5.92% from 5.1% in the prior-year period.
What's Changed
Net Profit turned around to ₹26.2 crore from a net loss of ₹10.4 crore YoY.
Revenue expanded by 24.63% YoY to ₹2,100 crore from ₹1,685 crore (derived: ₹2,100 cr vs ₹1,685 cr).
EBITDA increased by 44.54% YoY to ₹123 crore from ₹85.1 crore (derived: ₹123 cr vs ₹85.1 cr).
EBITDA Margin expanded by 82 bps YoY to 5.92% from 5.1%.
Key Takeaways
Q2 net profit of ₹26.2 crore beat analyst consensus estimates of ₹20.7 crore.
Strong top-line expansion of 24.63% YoY driven by robust growth across supply chain operations.
EBITDA margin expansion of 82 bps YoY highlights improving cost efficiency and operating leverage.
SAHI Perspective
The performance reflects structural recovery in Mahindra Logistics' core operations, driven by a combination of strong top-line scale and margin expansion. Overcoming last year's net loss through a ₹123 crore EBITDA execution demonstrates effective cost control and utilization across 3PL networks.
Market Implications
Positive earnings surprise relative to consensus estimates provides earnings visibility and reflects operational stabilization in third-party logistics and freight operations.
Trading Signals
Market Bias: Bullish
Turnaround to a net profit of ₹26.2 crore alongside a 24.63% YoY revenue jump to ₹2,100 crore and an 82 bps margin expansion underscores strong operational momentum.
Overweight: Logistics & Supply Chain, Third-Party Logistics (3PL)
Trigger Factors:
Sustained quarterly EBITDA margin expansion above 6%
Volume trajectory in core supply chain management solutions
Time Horizon: Near-term (0-3 months)
Industry Context
The Indian third-party logistics sector continues to benefit from demand stabilization across automotive, industrial, and consumer goods verticals, with operators prioritizing network optimization and cost discipline.
Key Risks to Watch
Potential fuel price volatility impacting transport operational margins
Uncertainty in discretionary consumer demand affecting express shipment volumes
Recent Developments
Mahindra Logistics scheduled its Board Meeting and earnings conference call for October 23, 2026, to review and approve the Q2 financial results.
Closing Insight
A beat on both top-line growth and net profit estimates establishes a stronger baseline for Mahindra Logistics as operating leverage continues to take effect across its logistics network.
